attribution.note: Marcus wrote this sentence in his own Substack essay, in his own voice. It is not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps the causal link (excluding scientists leaves the two companies as the only parties able to act on risks) and the target. It is argumentative, but its wording is unhedged.

contract.note: Reading the claim as of publication day and on its plain meaning is fair and ordinary. Requiring an independent, effective or enforceable outside intervention to contradict it, and more than restricted disclosure to support it, matches 'alone... do anything'.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own March 2023 report (a company disclosure). It confirms limited outside access: no fine-tuning, no final model, architecture details withheld. That backs the access premise but not the claim that outsiders could not act on risks.
OpenAI page (a company disclosure). Invited experts fed company-run mitigations. Under the contract this shows company-controlled consultation, not independent outside capacity.

Genuine NCSC blog dated 14 Mar 2023, but mislabelled as a company disclosure: it is a government agency publication. It advises users to be careful with data, a precaution with no measured effect, so it does not meet the contradiction condition.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows restricted outside access to GPT-4 (e1, e2), which matches Marcus's premise. Nothing establishes the causal part: that this restriction left outsiders unable to implement or compel measures against the risks. Nothing shows an effective independent intervention either; the NCSC advice (e3) is a precaution with no shown effect. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.
